- Consider discontinuation of any non-essential medications contributing to GI dysbiosis.

This is a classic presentation of antibiotic-associated diarrhea (AAD) with high pretest probability for *Clostridioides difficile* infection (CDI). The acute onset of watery diarrhea and lower abdominal cramping—without fever, vomiting, or systemic toxicity—is consistent with CDI, especially in the context of recent fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin) exposure, which is a well-documented high-risk antibiotic for CDI. Leukocytosis with neutrophilic predominance (WBC 13,400/mm³, 80% neutrophils) further supports an inflammatory/infectious colitis rather than simple osmotic or functional diarrhea. While absence of fever and hematochezia lowers suspicion for severe or fulminant CDI, it does not exclude mild-to-moderate CDI—many cases present precisely this way. - Absence of identifiable non-antibiotic epidemiologic exposures (travel, foodborne, contact)

Clostridioides difficile infection.
